source: Read [Rules](rules.md) and [Conventions](conventions.md) before selecting a mode.

A board's repositories are those its items' issues live in, read from each item's issue, deduplicated and ordered with the board's own repository first. An item whose issue is unreadable leaves the list incomplete, which is reported rather than filled by assumption.

The project's ordered long-lived branch names, declared in `config/branches` at its root, one name per line. A run reads the statement at the commit it evaluates, in the repository its checkout locates; which worktree the checkout is, and what its working files hold, choose nothing. The evaluated revision is fetched before it is read.
The complete set of Development links between those pull requests and the issues they deliver, read through the access that exposes them whole.

A unit is one task row or tasks that name each other in Joins, as [Work Breakdown](epic-issue-body.md#work-breakdown) defines. A unit of rows comes only from an epic that is Ready or In Progress in the supplied board items: the plan offers no other row, and none other is held. A [hot-fix unit](#hot-fix-units) has no row. One unit is one session's work, delivered by one pull request into each epic base it changes. Its first task id and Description determine the planning-folder identity, which every row of the unit is reserved with, and with each epic base it changes its branch and worktree, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) names them. In an epic of several bases, the bases a unit changes are read from the [Component](work-item.md#component) declaration of the work-item file each free row links, in the engineering worktree. A unit with a row linking no work item changes every epic base, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) states for unplanned rows.

Check one selected unit immediately before execution and provide [Validated Unit](#validated-unit "●") to the requester, or [Failure](#failure "●") if the operation fails. The start names one selected unit, has a currently free harness slot and overlaps no held or running session. Its supplied evidence names that unit, the planning record confirmed on the remote engineering branch, and the record associated with its confirmed hold. For rows, that association is read from every live row reservation; for a hot-fix it is the run's record for the unit whose board hold was confirmed. The evidence is gathered in that order before execution; any missing, mismatched or unverified evidence blocks the start.
- A closed epic is normalized to the current Work Breakdown columns before its tasks are read, using the shared format rules. Ambiguous or unsupported table content is a blocker.

The required-before-use graph contains only explicit prerequisite edges, each naming its entry condition, required content and reason. It must be acyclic for every supported entry path. Ordinary field references and intentional execution retries impose no prerequisite ordering. A selected link bounds the read; only an explicit execution call runs a linked procedure. Reuse complete context already received at the same revision.
Read this before adding or changing a mode, applying [SOLID](#solid).
Read this before adding or changing a protocol, applying [SOLID](#solid).
Read this before adding or changing an artifact, applying [SOLID](#solid).
Read this before adding or changing a reference, applying [SOLID](#solid).

- For delivery discrepancies, Apply [Read Delivery Evidence](../artifacts/delivery-evidence.md#read-delivery-evidence "ƒ") for the selected repositories and initiative against current issue records, then repeat this survey with its refreshed evidence before selecting a dispatch batch.
Read the [shared skill guidelines](../../guidelines.md) and [skill guidelines](../guidelines.md) whole before the first edit.
- Apply [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue "ƒ") for each selected issue before inspecting its Open Questions or format.

- Apply [Read Tracker Issue](../artifacts/issue.md#read-tracker-issue "ƒ") for the originating proposal identified in the initiative's [References](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#references); provide unresolved provenance before board creation for a proposal-derived initiative.

- For any failed gate or called operation through handoff, Apply [Hold Epic Review](../artifacts/pull-request.md#hold-epic-review "ƒ") and Apply [Record Epic Review](../artifacts/board-delivery.md#record-epic-review "ƒ") again with their preceding inputs before returning or retrying, including failures between ready and board writes. The confirmed absence of a board is the sole exception to board withdrawal.

- Apply [Fetch Merge Readiness](../artifacts/pull-request.md#fetch-merge-readiness "ƒ") for the exact current head and target. A conflict, failed or pending check, unmet epic condition or incomplete evidence blocks handoff; Apply [Hold Epic Review](../artifacts/pull-request.md#hold-epic-review "ƒ") again and Apply [Record Epic Review](../artifacts/board-delivery.md#record-epic-review "ƒ") requesting In Progress before returning that blocker. Pending required human approval is provided to the next step as a human handoff, with merge blocked.
- For a new unit of rows, read each component from the work-item file its free row links, before reservation replaces that link.
- Apply [Read Board State](../artifacts/board.md#read-board-state "ƒ") for the selected board immediately before acquiring the unit's hold.

Read a heading-linked section and its subsections, stopping before the next heading of equal or higher level. Follow in-text links as their context is needed for the selected work. Preserve boundaries in batched reads and recover truncated output. Reuse complete context already read at the same revision. Explicit whole-document requirements still apply.
